sample_unit: radiology residents (240 case readings across 40 brain MRI cases)
models_evaluated: LLM-based search engine and hybrid chatbot

links.outcome: Reader differential diagnosis accuracy with LLM assistance versus conventional internet search
links.effect: 70/114 (61.4%) correct with LLM assistance vs 53/114 (46.5%) conventional, p = 0.033; no difference in interpretation time or confidence.
links.quote: LLM-assisted brain MRI differential diagnosis yielded superior accuracy (70/114; 61.4% (LLM-assisted) vs 53/114; 46.5% (conventional) correct diagnoses, p = 0.033, chi-square test).

links.outcome: LLM hallucinations and their propagation into reader responses
links.effect: LLM hallucinations occurred in 11.5% of cases; correct LLM suggestions translated into correct reader responses in 82.1% (60/73).
links.quote: Inaccurate case descriptions by readers (9.2% of cases), LLM hallucinations (11.5% of cases), and insufficient contextualization of LLM responses were identified as challenges related to human-LLM interaction.

screen.reason: Evaluates the impact of an LLM-assisted search/differential diagnosis workflow versus conventional search on radiology resident diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in a crossover reader study.

primary.practice: LLM assistance for diagnostic search vs conventional search
